After replacing a couple of different filters my filter still had a leak. I thought it was the filter but ended up not bing the problem. I did the repair shown on U tube on cleaning out  the hose connection fittings and o rings. No change. I had come to the conclusion it was the small valve used to open and close the filter bypass passage. The plastic pin on the filter pushes it in to direct the water through the filter. It was leaking past the o ring and into the holder. This new replacement took care of my problem . NOT cheap, but what else is one to do.

Inserting a new filter resulted in water coming from the dispenser in a trickle. Online troubleshooting led me to this filter housing as a solution. I used this part and it immediately fixed my issue.

Things to know to make the install easier: the old filter lines only come off the original filter housing if you are pressing down on the grey rings that hold them in place, you don't just pull hard. An open ended wrench can be used to do this easily. This is MUCH easier to install if you loosen the water line mount on the back of the refrigerator first. Search Youtube for videos that show exactly how to do both these things. I tried to wing it at first because it looks very simple (and it is) but I would have been done in 10 minutes flat if I had just watched a video before I started, even though I didn't think I would need to.

After looking into this I found this part that will speed up the water dispenser on older Whirlpool Fridge with the push button filter at the bottom. It was taking my fridge 42 seconds to fill 16 oz of water after replacing this part it only took 16 seconds to fill 16 oz. You don’t realize how slow it really was until you fix it.

Replacing the part is fairly easy, just take your time and be methodical about. There are videos online that show the procedure.

Last time hubby replaced the filter, the filter housing broke. Purchased this part and it did the trick. Saved us $1000’s from having to purchase a new fridge.
